Former slaveowner John Brown Gordon survived the Civil War to become the leader of the Ku Klux Klan in Georgia despite taking five bullets at Antietam in 1862 and three more wounds in different engagements as he progressed from captain to major general in the Confederate army.
As a member of the U.S. Senate, Gordon helped negotiate the end of Reconstruction in 1877, which rehabilitated the white Southern elite and permitted a new age of racial tyranny to arise. A two-term governor of Georgia, Gordon was also the first commander of the United Confederate Veterans.
The position was formerly named after General John Gordon, but on Friday morning, just outside of Augusta, a ceremony took place honoring Dwight D. Eisenhower. Eisenhower was a five-star commander during World War II who helped lead the downfall of Nazi Germany and a president who supervised significant racial integration achievements. When Arkansas's governor tried to prevent nine Black students from enrolling at Little Rock Central High School in 1957, Eisenhower sent the 101st Airborne Division and federalized the state's National Guard.
Members of the former president's family were in attendance, and Army Secretary Christine Wormuth gave a statement lauding Eisenhower's accomplishments.
In a nearly three-year process that began when Congress established the bipartisan Naming Commission in the fiscal 2021 defense policy bill to rename the military's locations and objects that honored Confederates, the Army completed its final installation-level renaming on Friday. The final redesignation took place at Eisenhower, and four members of the commission were present.
In his speech, Wormuth noted that the renaming process arose from the "unrest and significant division in our country" that arose after the 2020 killing of George Floyd spurred racial justice rallies. The new namesakes, however, "unquestionably represent" the qualities the Army seeks in its future soldiers and leaders, which she praised.
Retired Army Brigadier General Ty Seidule, the commission's vice chair, shared these sentiments in a phone interview on Wednesday.
True American heroes... who uphold the ideals of our great nation should be honored at any time in their lives, he said.
However, more than only the names were altered. More than 1,100 Defense Department items, from the USS Chancellorsville to street names, had their labels deemed worthy of reevaluation by the Naming Commission, changing the memorial landscape of military stations around the United States.

Linear Bus topology is a type of network where all nodes are connected to a single transmission medium with two endpoints. Distributed Bus topology is similar to Linear Bus topology, but in this case, the transmission medium has more than two endpoints created by branching the main section of the transmitting medium. 

Star topology is another type of network where each computer is connected to a central hub using a point-to-point connection. This type of network is not usually used for large networks, such as those covering an entire building, due to difficulty in troubleshooting.

Mesh topology introduces the concept of routes, where messages sent on a mesh network can take any of several possible paths from source to destination. Some Wide Area Networks (WANs), most notably the Internet, employ mesh routing.

answer:
Sure! Here are brief explanations of each type of network topology mentioned in the passages:

1. Linear Bus: In a Linear Bus topology, all network nodes are connected to a common transmission medium via two endpoints. This topology is simple to install and maintain but can be prone to single points of failure, meaning that if one node fails, the entire network will be affected.
2. Distributed Bus: In a Distributed Bus topology, all network nodes are connected to a shared transmission medium via multiple endpoints, creating a branched structure. This topology is similar to the Linear Bus topology but offers greater redundancy and reliability due to the multiple connections.
3. Star: In a Star topology, each computer or device is connected to a central hub using a point-to-point connection. This topology is easy to manage and maintain, and the central hub provides a single point of failure, making it easier to troubleshoot issues. However, this topology can become expensive as more devices need to be connected to the central hub.
4. Mesh: In a Mesh topology, each device is directly connected to every other device in the network, forming a web-like structure. This topology offers high redundancy and reliability as there are multiple paths for data to travel between devices. Additionally, mesh networks can self-heal, meaning that if one path becomes unavailable, data can be rerouted through another path.

answer: Preheat the oven to 500 degrees F. Place the beef filet on a sheet pan and pat the outside dry with a paper towel. Spread butter on with your hands and sprinkle evenly with salt and pepper. Roast in the oven for exactly 22 minutes for rare and 25 minutes for medium-rare. For a steak cooked to medium, cook the filet for 2 to 7 minutes until the meat reaches a temperature of at least 140 degrees. For medium-well, cook for 4 to 9 minutes until it reaches a temperature of at least 150 degrees. Turn the filet mignon once about halfway through the cooking time. Remove the filet from the oven and place it on a carving board. Cover the meat loosely with aluminum foil and allow it to rest for 5 to 10 minutes. Carve the meat and transfer it to a warm serving platter.

answer: To cook a beef tip roast in the oven, first preheat the oven to 500°. Make cuts in the fat of the beef in a diamond pattern. Combine flour, salt, garlic salt, and pepper then rub the roast all over with this mixture. Put the roast on a rack in a shallow baking pan and place it in the oven, reducing the heat to 475°. Roast for about 7 minutes per pound or 30 minutes. Turn off the heat and leave the roast in the oven for 2 1/2 hours. Do not open the oven until you're ready to carve and serve. Cook for about 25 minutes per pound or approximately 50 to 60 minutes. Use a meat thermometer to check doneness, which should read 140° for medium. Let the roast rest for 15 minutes before carving.

answer: Preheat your oven to 350°F (175 degrees C). Wash and peel the sweet potatoes, then cut them into medium size pieces. Coat the bottom of a baking dish with just enough olive oil to cover it. Place the cut sweet potatoes in the dish and turn them so they are coated with the oil. You can then season them with oregano, salt, and pepper to taste. Alternatively, you can mix brown sugar and pumpkin pie spice in a large bowl, add the sweet potatoes and toss well. Spread them in a 13x9-inch baking dish, pour a mix of orange juice and vanilla over them, and dot with butter. Cover and bake for 40 minutes, then stir and bake uncovered for another 15 to 20 minutes or until they are fork tender. Another method is to bake for 60 minutes or until they are soft.

On the other hand, lice are wingless insects that infest the hair and scalp, feeding on human blood which can cause an itchy scalp and occasionally an allergic reaction. Lice are spread through contact with others, particularly head to head contact or sharing of head accessories and garments. Nits, which are often confused with dandruff, are eggs of lice laid by female lice and are found on the hair shafts. The methods of prevention and treatment also differ between lice and dandruff.

answer:
To boil a lobster at home, follow these steps:

1. Fill a large pot with enough water to cover the lobsters, adding sea salt or regular salt and any desired flavorings (such as lemon slices, wine, beer, thyme, or bay leaves) to the water.
2. Preheat the broiler.
3. Carefully cut the top side of the lobster shells lengthwise and pull apart the shells slightly. Season the lobster meat with butter, paprika, salt, and white pepper.
4. Place the lobster tails in the pot, making sure they are completely covered by the water.
5. Cover the pot and bring the water to a boil.
6. Reduce the heat and let the lobsters simmer for 8-10 minutes, or until the meat is opaque and cooked through.
7. Remove the lobsters from the pot and serve with melted butter.

Note: You can also steam the lobsters instead of boiling them. To do this, pour about 1 inch of water in the bottom of a large pot, add the salt, and place a steamer insert inside the pot. Place the lobster tails on the rack and cover the pot. Cover and steam for 8 minutes.

answer: To safely drain your pool, first, turn off the power to the pool's filtration system at the circuit breaker and turn off the automatic water fill valve. Then, locate the sewer clean-out port to access the sanitary sewer line. A drainage hose should be run from the sewer clean-out port to the pool and connected to a submersible pump. This pump should be lowered into the deepest area of the pool, near the drain. As you drain, monitor the flow into the clean-out port to ensure water doesn't back up into your home's sink and shower drains. It may be wise to hire a professional if your pool has a vinyl liner, but if you are confident in your pool's ability to withstand the draining process, you can rent a sump pump and connect it to the sewer drainage pipe instead. Place the pump in the deepest part of the pool and turn it on.

There are two methods shared in the passages to remove rust from old tools. The first method involves making a solution of salt and lemon juice. This can be rubbed onto the tools with steel wool or a scourging pad. The salt acts as an abrasive and the acid in the lemon juice cuts through the rust. For heavily rusted tools, the solution should be left on the surface for a few minutes before wiping clean with a dry rag.

The second method uses vinegar. The rusty tools should be put in a bowl and covered with vinegar. If the rust is thick, the tools may need to remain in the vinegar for up to two days. After removal from the vinegar, the rust will have turned into a viscous film that can be cleaned off with a strong water jet. If any rust remains, it can be removed with a wire brush. Finally, the tools should be washed with soap and water to remove any traces of vinegar.

8. Set the appropriate water temperature and cycle based on the clothing type.
9. Add the detergent and start the washing machine.
10. Once the washing cycle is complete, transfer the clothes to the dryer or hang them to air dry.

answer: A registered trademark, identified with the symbol ®, is a federally and legally registered mark that is protected from use by other companies. If another company uses a similar image, they can be accused of trademark infringement. On the other hand, an unregistered trademark is a mark enforced and created by a business or individual to signify or distinguish a product or service in the market. It does not provide strong security for the product or service, but it does have some common law rights even without registration.

answer: A registered trademark is a mark that has been legally registered with the appropriate authorities and is designated with the symbol ®. answer: The Paleo diet is a nutritional approach designed to work with human genetics to promote lean physique and high energy levels. It is a matter of debate in the Paleo community whether starchy vegetables, particularly potatoes, are allowed, with some advocates saying true root vegetables are acceptable but not regular potatoes and other tubers. There is also controversy over the consumption of grains like wheat, rice, or corn, which are not only difficult to digest in their raw states, but can be toxic.
context:
passage 1:The Paleo diet is the healthiest way you can eat because it is the ONLY nutritional approach that works with your genetics to help you stay lean, strong and energetic!

passage 2:Potatoes & Starchy Vegetables. Starchy vegetables, potatoes in particular, are a matter of some debate when it comes to the Paleo Diet. Many advocates say true root vegetables like carrots and sweet potatoes are okay, but regular potatoes and other tubers are not. Others say any starchy vegetable is okay in moderation.

passage 3:Taking front and center of the Paleo controversy is whether you should even be eating things like wheat, rice or corn, let alone making them the base of your food pyramid. Paleo advocates will point out that grains are not only difficult for humans to digest in their raw states, but they can actually be quite toxic.

answer: The key points of the Paleo diet are that it is based on genetics, helps in staying lean, strong and energetic, allows for the consumption of true root vegetables like carrots and sweet potatoes but not regular potatoes and other tubers, and discourages the consumption of grains like wheat, rice, and corn due to difficulties in digestion and potential toxicity.

answer: Phosphorus is the second most abundant mineral in the human body, with about 85% of it found in the bones and teeth. It works closely with calcium to build strong bones and teeth. In addition to this, phosphorus is found in cells and tissues throughout the body, and plays a crucial role in filtering out waste in the kidneys and in how the body stores and uses energy. It also helps to reduce muscle pain after intense physical activity. However, an imbalance of phosphorus and calcium in the body can lead to health problems such as osteoporosis, as well as gum and teeth issues. Therefore, maintaining a balanced dietary intake of calcium and phosphorus is important.

answer: The exercises that help reduce belly fat include various forms of crunches, particularly reverse crunches. These exercises involve tilting the legs behind simultaneously with the shoulders, which is especially effective for targeting lower belly fat. Another variation includes lying faceup with knees bent to 90 degrees, hands behind the head, and abs contracted. Then, while keeping knees stacked over hips, lift the shoulders and crunch up, hold for 3-5 seconds, exhale and extend legs to 45 degrees, hold for 3-5 seconds while squeezing the lower belly. This should be performed in 2 sets of 10-15 reps.

Based on the given passages, here is a brief recipe for turkey fennel meatloaf:

Ingredients:

* 1 lb ground turkey
* 1/2 cup breadcrumbs
* 1/2 cup ketchup
* 1/4 cup chopped onion
* 2 cloves garlic, minced
* 1/4 cup chopped celery
* 1/4 cup chopped fennel
* 1 egg
* Salt and pepper, to taste
* Hot sauce (optional)

1. Preheat oven to 375°F with rack positioned in center of oven.
2. In a large bowl, combine ground turkey, breadcrumbs, ketchup, onion, garlic, celery, fennel, egg, salt, and pepper. Mix well.
3. Press the mixture into an 8x4-inch loaf pan.
4. Bake for 45-50 minutes or until the meatloaf is browned on top, cooked through, and an instant-read thermometer inserted in the center registers 165°F.
5. If desired, top with barbecue sauce before baking.

answer: To make a chimney cap, first measure the top of the chimney, and the length, width, and height of the flue. Use these measurements to build the bottom of the mold out of ¾-inch plywood. Add 2 inches to the measurements so that the cap will overhang the chimney by 2 inches on all sides. Cut the plywood to this measurement using a table saw or circular saw, and create a cutout for the flue. Once this is done, place the cap over the crown of the chimney, ensuring it's centered over the top flue. There's no need for a perfect fit as the cap essentially cages in the chimney. Use adhesive or Tapcon masonry anchors to secure the cap. If using anchors, you'll need a 3/16 masonry bit and enough Tapcon screws to mount your cap. Choose screws that are ¼ diameter and 1 ½ or 1 ¾ long. Finally, invest in a stainless steel cap as it offers several advantages such as preventing excess rain, snow, wind, birds, and other animals from entering your chimney.

answer: Struts and shocks are both components of a vehicle's suspension system, but they have different structures and functions. A strut is essentially a shock absorber and a spring combined into one unit, and it provides structural support for the vehicle. In addition to absorbing shocks from the road, struts also have steering elements and support the vehicle's weight. Struts are more commonly found on cars. On the other hand, a shock absorber, also known as a damper, is a device that absorbs vibrations from the springs that have absorbed the shocks on the road. Shocks do not provide any structural support for the vehicle and are most commonly found on trucks, SUVs, and vans. Shocks are simpler and less expensive than struts because they only resist the bouncing of the vehicle using hydraulics.

This shift led to significant urbanization as people moved from rural areas to cities. The introduction of machines for laborious work and the replacement of animal labor with human labor characterized this period. The second phase of the Industrial Revolution, starting in the 1860s, saw significant advancements in the production of steel, railroads, electricity, and chemicals, characterized by mass-production and consumption of goods. However, this period also brought about longer work hours for the working class, leaving little time or energy for recreation.

4. Uncheck the Locked box and click OK.

7. Click Review Protect Sheet, enter a password (if desired), and click OK.
8. If you want to protect the sheet, repeat step 7 and click OK.
9. Users will no longer be able to copy and paste into any locked cells on the worksheet.

answer: To cook eggs without sticking, start with medium heat and let the pan get hot. Before it gets too hot, add a tablespoon of butter. Once the foaming stops, add the eggs into the pan and stir constantly, but reduce the heat to low. Add about a tablespoon of milk to the eggs. If the eggs start sticking to the bottom, the pan has gotten too hot - move it off the burner and continue stirring. Alternatively, you can coat the bottom of the pan with nonstick cooking spray or butter. If using butter, rub it into the bottom of the pan and leave the remainder in the pan. Place the pan over medium heat and prepare the eggs. For scrambled eggs, crack the eggs into a bowl, beat them with a fork or a whisk and add seasonings.

answer: To make good pancakes, whisk together 1 1/2 cups flour, 3 tablespoons sugar, 1 1/2 teaspoons baking powder, 1/2 teaspoon salt and 1/4 teaspoon baking soda in a medium bowl. In a separate bowl, combine 1 cup plus 2 tablespoons milk, 4 tablespoons melted butter and 1 egg. Fold this wet mixture into the flour mixture until just combined, it's okay if there are some lumps. Heat a large nonstick skillet or griddle over medium-low heat, brushing it with butter. Add ¼ cupfuls of batter and cook until bubbly on top and golden on the bottom, about 4 minutes. Flip the pancakes and cook until golden on the other side, about 2 more minutes. To make them extra special, you can top the pancakes with sliced bananas, chocolate sauce, granola, and/or bacon-pecan syrup. To make the syrup, cook 4 strips of bacon until crisp, then crumble. Drain all but 1 tablespoon of the drippings, add 1/2 cup chopped pecans and cook for 2 minutes. Add 1½ cups maple syrup, the cooked bacon, and 1/4 teaspoon cider vinegar, then heat through. Serve the pancakes hot.
